original_question: Let Omega be a bounded hyperconvex domain in C^n, and let u be the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function on Omega with boundary value 0 and Monge-Ampere equation (dd^c u)^n = f dV, where f is smooth and bounded below by a positive constant. Determine whether u is automatically smooth.
target_in_paper: Question 23 (Blocki) in Section 3.5, “Pogorelov interior estimate”: let Ω⊂ℂ^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain, let u be the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function with u|∂Ω=0 and (dd^c u)^n=f dV for smooth f bounded away from zero, and ask whether u is automatically smooth. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact problem in the paper almost verbatim: the ambient space Ω⊂ℂ^n, the assumption that Ω is bounded and hyperconvex, the zero Dirichlet boundary condition, the unknown u as the unique continuous plurisubharmonic solution, the equation (dd^c u)^n=f dV, the hypothesis that f is smooth and strictly positive, and the regularity question asking whether u is automatically smooth. This is precisely the content of Question 23. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper explicitly defines “hyperconvex”: there exists a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion ρ on Ω such that each sublevel set {ρ<c} is relatively compact in Ω for every c<0. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To make the boundary condition fully explicit, u should be understood as plurisubharmonic on Ω and continuous up to the boundary, with u=0 on ∂Ω. The paper phrases this as “the unique continuous plurisubharmonic function in Ω such that u|∂Ω=0.” ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The equation should be understood in the pluripotential/Bedford–Taylor sense for continuous plurisubharmonic functions, not only as a classical determinant identity. The introduction defines MA(ϕ)=(dd^cϕ)^n and recalls Bedford–Taylor well-definedness for locally bounded psh functions. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The draft leaves dV implicit; in the paper, dV is the Lebesgue volume form on ℂ^n. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The paper states the positivity assumption as “f smooth and bounded away from zero,” i.e. there exists ε>0 such that f≥ε>0. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The normalization of dd^c is left implicit in the draft; the paper’s local convention is the standard one consistent with dd^c‖z‖^2=∑(i/π)dz_j∧d\bar z_j. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

For paper-faithful standalone wording, the intended conclusion is interior smoothness on Ω (C^∞ on Ω), not boundary smoothness up to ∂Ω; the paper treats boundary-regularity questions separately in the following subsection. This is a context-based inference from Sections 3.5–3.6. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω⊂ℂ^n be a bounded hyperconvex domain, meaning that there exists a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion ρ on Ω such that {ρ<c} is relatively compact in Ω for every c<0. Let dV denote Lebesgue measure on ℂ^n, and use the paper’s standard normalization dd^c=(i/π)∂∂̄. Suppose u is the unique plurisubharmonic function on Ω that extends continuously to ∂Ω, satisfies u=0 on ∂Ω, and solves (dd^c u)^n=f dV in Ω in the Bedford–Taylor sense, where f is smooth and bounded away from zero (equivalently, f≥ε>0 for some ε>0). Must u be C^∞ on Ω? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 3.5 rather than a neighboring problem: it reproduces Question 23 (Blocki) essentially word-for-word. The same page supplies the hidden definition of hyperconvexity and the nearby remarks explain the intended scope: no a priori regularity of ∂Ω is assumed, the problem is still open even when f is constant, it is known for smooth strongly pseudoconvex domains, and the missing ingredient is a complex analogue of Pogorelov’s interior C^2 estimate. This confirms that the sharp paper-faithful formulation is exactly the bounded-hyperconvex Dirichlet problem above, without broadening to other domains or to stronger regularity hypotheses such as those in Question 24. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
